title: The Cranes in Tense Times
summary: How the Resplendent Cranes hold to the old ways.

claims.text: In tense nights the Resplendent Cranes still cling to the ancient ways, valuing obedience to law and elders.
They keep stressing the schooling of new Kuei-jin, both in scripture and tenets and in the means to fight the corruption around them.

title: Crane Jina as Teachers
summary: When a Crane is ready to teach.

claims.text: A Crane is ready to teach on reaching ling and becoming jina, having grasped righteousness well enough to know a place within the laws of Heaven and live without strain.
Old tales tell of one great master taking many pupils.

title: Crane Sects
summary: How the Way of the Resplendent Crane is organized.

claims.text: Elder mandarins run the sects, younger mandarins lead temple services with jina assisting, and Running Monkeys report to everyone with little say; rank in a sect follows enlightenment.

Several sects stray from the orthodoxy of the Shining Ice Guardians of the Blood Court yet remain accepted parts of the Dharma, stressing different tenets without opposing the rest; their quarrels have still led to shadow wars.
The Eight Lotuses Blooming sect traces its tradition to the Southern Song, when Neo-Confucianism arose.

title: The Yellow Moon
summary: A small Crane sect born of a heresy charge.

claims.text: When three great mandarins brought an innovation the core of the Dharma disliked, the ancestors stripped them of their posts for heresy.
The three founded their own sect, the Yellow Moon, which for a long time had no other members; they studied texts, memorized koans and debated contentedly.

title: The Sisters of the Cooling Hearth
summary: One of the oldest Crane wu.

claims.text: Among the oldest Crane wu, the Sisters of the Cooling Hearth admit only female, gender-neutral or androgynous members.
They do not welcome males, though they will advise groups of male Kuei-jin.
